findings.issue: _rewrite_action classifies only actions that START with rebase, reset or filter-branch. The old substring test also caught a rebase run through another command, whose reflog action is the caller's GIT_REFLOG_ACTION, such as `pull --rebase (finish): ...` (from my knowledge of git, not observed here). Under the new test that entry is not a rewrite verb. The ancestry test still catches a rebase that moves the tip off its old line. A rebase that lands on a descendant of the old tip, the case the verb match exists for, is no longer named when it came through `pull --rebase`. rw1-rw6 cover no such entry.
findings.resolution: Match the verb inside the action as well as at its start, for example a word-boundary test for `rebase` over `action` (the text before the first ': '), and add an rw case with the message `pull --rebase (finish): returning to refs/heads/x`. A commit subject stays out of reach because only the action is searched.
